items.title: AI-DRIVEN PRECISION ONCOLOGY: REVOLUTIONIZING PERSONALIZED CANCER THERAPY
items.abstract: Precision oncology is an approach in which cancer treatment is selected according to the molecular, genomic and clinical characteristics of an individual patient and tumour. Artificial intelligence (AI), including machine learning, deep learning and natural language processing, can analyses large and complex datasets generated by genomics, pathology, radiology and electronic health records. AI may help identify actionable biomarkers, predict treatment response and resistance, support drug discovery, match patients to clinical trials and anticipate adverse drug reactions (ADRs). This review describes the principles of AI-driven precision oncology, major biomarkers, pharmacogenomics, mechanisms of selected targeted and immune therapies, drug-specific adverse effects, AI-assisted toxicity prediction, clinical workflow, advantages, limitations, ethical considerations and future directions. Selected therapies including osimertinib, trastuzumab, dabrafenib/trametinib, olaparib and pembrolizumab demonstrate how molecular findings can be translated into individualized treatment. The future of oncology is likely to involve multimodal AI combined with longitudinal molecular monitoring and multidisciplinary clinical decision-making.

items.title: AI-Enabled Animal Behavior Analysis for Translational Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery
items.abstract: Animal behavior is a critical endpoint in preclinical pharmacology, toxicology, and therapeutic discovery, yet conventional behavioral scoring remains labor-intensive, low-dimensional, and difficult to reproduce across laboratories. Artificial intelligence (AI) can now quantify behavior from video with greater spatial, temporal, and phenotypic resolution. This review summarizes how object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, foundation models, and autonomous analysis agents are reshaping behavioral phenotyping. General-purpose object detectors rapidly localize and track animals, whereas open-source pose-estimation tools extend measurement beyond centroid tracking to body-part trajectories and fine motor patterns; paired with supervised classifiers, they have matched human scoring and exceeded some commercial systems. Technical accuracy alone does not establish behavioral construct validity or pharmacological validity. Unsupervised methods such as Motion Sequencing represent drug responses and disease-model phenotypes as structured changes in behavioral states rather than only as predefined endpoints, providing high-dimensional fingerprints of pharmacological action. Segmentation and tracking foundation models may reduce annotation burden but require validation across species, strain, sex, apparatus, and paradigm. AI agents may assist with literature review, code generation, analysis auditing, and figure production but must remain within transparent, human-supervised workflows. In behavioral pharmacology, pose estimation is established as a measurement method and emerging as a drug-effect endpoint, supervised classification and unsupervised segmentation are emerging, and foundation models and agents remain prospective. AI-enabled behavioral analysis can become a reproducible phenotyping layer for drug discovery and toxicology if researchers adopt open pipelines, rigorous validation, and reporting standards, rather than replacing one opaque measurement system with another.

items.title: AI-Enabled Assistive Ecosystems
items.abstract: Higher education institutions worldwide are increasingly prioritizing inclusive learning environments that accommodate the diverse needs of students with disabilities. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have introduced transformative opportunities for developing assistive ecosystems that support accessibility, personalized learning, and institutional efficiency. AI-enabled technologies—including intelligent tutoring systems, speech recognition, computer vision, and predictive analytics—can significantly enhance disability support services while improving educational outcomes and institutional performance. This chapter explores the concept of AI-enabled assistive ecosystems within higher education and examines how integrated AI technologies can support students with physical, sensory, cognitive, and learning disabilities. The chapter analyzes the potential benefits of AI-driven accessibility tools, institutional data analytics, and adaptive learning platforms for promoting inclusive education.

items.title: AI-Enabled Compliance Monitoring and Adherence to Financial Regulations in Nigeria's Federal Public Sector
items.abstract: Compliance with financial regulations is central to public accountability, yet monitoring adherence across ministries, departments and agencies is difficult at the scale and complexity of Nigeria's federal public sector. This study examines whether documented adoption of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled compliance monitoring is associated with adherence to financial regulations in Nigeria's federal public sector. A balanced panel of five federal institutions, the Federal Ministry of Finance, the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation, the Federal Inland Revenue Service, the Central Bank of Nigeria and the Bureau of Public Procurement is observed over 2015–2024. Documentary evidence from annual reports, audit-related documents and AI-implementation documents is scored on a five-point (0–4) rubric and analysed with pooled, fixed-effects, trend-adjusted, first-difference and lagged regressions, interpreted through agency theory. AI-enabled compliance monitoring is positively and significantly associated with regulatory compliance (pooled β = 0.719, R² = 0.923; fixed-effects β = 0.742, within R² = 0.858). The association remains positive and significant after controlling for a common time trend (β = 0.629), in first differences (β = 0.554) and when monitoring is lagged one year (β = 0.657). A conservative reading is that one additional point of monitoring adoption is associated with roughly 0.55 to 0.65 points higher regulatory compliance. Because the design is observational, the measures are documentary indices, and the sample is small and purposively selected, the results indicate association rather than proven causation and are interpreted for the five institutions examined rather than for all federal ministries, departments and agencies. The findings support investment in AI-enabled monitoring as one component of a functioning compliance chain, accompanied by data quality, regulatory clarity, staff capacity, governance arrangements and human review.

items.title: AI-Enabled Disability Support in Higher Education
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence is transforming disability support in higher education by enabling personalization, predictive analytics, and systemic change. This chapter explores AI tools—such as adaptive learning platforms, NLP assistants, early-alert systems, and automated accommodations—used to address barriers faced by students with diverse disabilities. Grounded in Universal Design for Learning and the social model of disability, it reframes AI as a means to enhance student autonomy rather than just improve services. It also examines risks like algorithmic bias, surveillance, and data misuse. The chapter proposes a governance framework emphasizing equity, transparency, and student agency, and outlines key directions for future research.

items.title: AI-Enabled Patient Profiling for Personalized Nursing Care and Health Support: Scoping Review
items.abstract: BACKGROUND AI-enabled patient profiling has been proposed to organize heterogeneous patient data and support personalized nursing care and health support. Given the growing use of AI, machine learning, large language models (LLMs), digital phenotyping, and digital twins in health care, it is important to clarify how patient profiling has been conceptualized, applied, and evaluated in nursing-relevant contexts. OBJECTIVE This scoping review aimed to examine and report the available evidence on AI-enabled patient profiling for personalized nursing care and health support. METHODS This scoping review was conducted using the Joanna Briggs Institute methodological framework and the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews). Chinese and English databases were searched from inception to May 18, 2026, including China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Data, VIP Database, Chinese Biomedical Literature Database, PubMed, CINAHL, Web of Science, and Embase. Eligible studies used AI or computational intelligence methods to construct, classify, apply, validate, or evaluate patient profiles or related patient representations relevant to personalized nursing care or health support. Two reviewers independently screened records, assessed full texts, and charted data using a predefined form. Data were synthesized descriptively and narratively using an input-process-output framework. RESULTS A total of 61 studies were included. AI-enabled patient profiling was represented through patient profiles, patient or user personas, digital phenotypes, patient segments, clinical subtypes, digital twins, and LLM-enabled personalization. Included studies used diverse data sources, including electronic health records, nursing records, patient-reported outcomes, questionnaires, mobile app data, wearable and sensor data, engagement logs, and textual or conversational data. Common AI approaches included machine learning, clustering, deep learning, natural language processing, recommender systems, knowledge graphs, digital twin modeling, and LLMs. Applications focused on personalized education, self-management support, rehabilitation, chronic disease management, remote monitoring, decision support, follow-up care, and shared decision-making. Most studies evaluated algorithmic performance, feasibility, usability, or system development, whereas fewer studies examined profile validity, actionability, equity, workflow integration, or long-term nursing-sensitive and patient-centered outcomes. CONCLUSIONS Existing evidence positions AI-enabled patient profiling as an emerging data-to-action mechanism for personalized nursing care and health support rather than as a mature clinical intervention. Future research should strengthen conceptual clarity, validate the profile, establish explicit pathways linking profiles to actions, incorporate nurse and patient involvement, assess equity and safety, and evaluate implementation in real-world nursing settings. items.title: AI-Enhanced Assignment Grading in Higher Education
items.abstract: The digitalization of education is critical for educational modernization and equitable access to quality education. However, higher education institutions face significant challenges in homework grading due to large student enrollments, including low grading efficiency and insufficient personalized feedback. This paper presents a general multi-agent framework leveraging large language models for automated assignment grading in higher education. The framework employed seven specialized agents: document reader, format converter, parser, artificial intelligence grading, data aggregation, report generation, and error handling. This domain-agnostic framework can be adapted to various disciplines by configuring appropriate grading criteria. A case study across nine classes with 258 students demonstrated 14–39 times efficiency improvement, reducing single-class processing time from 32–63 minutes to 1.6–2.3 minutes. The results indicated that the approach significantly reduced teachers' workload while providing targeted feedback, advancing digital transformation in education.

items.title: AI-Powered Predictive Analytics and Its Relationship with Budgeting Efficiency and Financial Accountability in Nigeria's Federal Public Sector
items.abstract: Budgets are the plans against which public financial reports are judged, and weak forecasting undermines both budget credibility and accountability. This study examines whether documented adoption of artificial intelligence (AI)-powered predictive analytics is associated with budgeting efficiency and financial accountability in Nigeria's federal public sector. A balanced panel of five federal institutions, the Federal Ministry of Finance, the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation, the Federal Inland Revenue Service, the Central Bank of Nigeria and the Bureau of Public Procurement, is observed over 2015–2024. Documentary evidence from annual reports, audit-related documents and AI-implementation documents is scored on a five-point (0–4) rubric and analysed with pooled, fixed-effects, trend-adjusted, first-difference and lagged regressions, interpreted through agency theory. Predictive analytics adoption is positively and significantly associated with budgeting efficiency and accountability (pooled β = 0.694, R² = 0.853; fixed-effects β = 0.712, within R² = 0.845). The association remains significant after adjusting for a common trend (β = 0.639), in first differences (β = 0.727) and with a one-year lag (β = 0.585). The lagged estimate is the smallest of the specifications, consistent with, though not proof of, a maturation period during which models learn from data and users learn to rely on forecasts. Because the design is observational, the measures are documentary indices, and the sample is small and purposively selected, the results indicate association rather than proven causation and are interpreted for the five institutions examined rather than for all federal ministries, departments and agencies. The results support investment in forecasting capability and data infrastructure, with realistic expectations about time-to-benefit, accompanied by data-quality programmes, staff training, publication of forecast errors and expert review of model outputs.

items.title: AI-Powered Predictive Analytics for Early Identification of Learning Disabilities
items.abstract: Learning disabilities (LDs) need to be identified at an early age so that they can be addressed promptly so that they can utilize their academic performance and inclusive learning. Conventional diagnostic procedures are mostly reactive, time-consuming and subjective and rely on the use of standardized tests, teacher observations, as well as, clinical evaluations. The development of artificial intelligence (AI) and predictive analytics allows active risk screening based on machine learning and deep learning, and explainable AI models. This chapter investigates predictive pipelines, benchmarking models (SVM) and random forests, (CNN and LSTM) and validation, ethics, privacy, and adaptive intervention frameworks in an attempt to encourage equitable, transparent, and scalable learning intervention systems.

items.title: AI-Supported Inclusive Teaching, Learning, and Assessment Practices
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming educational systems, offering innovative pathways for enhancing inclusive teaching, learning and assessment practices. In the context of disability support, AI-driven tools provide opportunities to personalize instruction, improve accessibility and strengthen institutional performance through data-informed decision-making. However, despite these potentials, some educational institutions face challenges in effectively integrating AI into inclusive education practices. This chapter therefore examines how AI-supported instructional strategies, adaptive learning systems and intelligent assessment tools can address diverse learner needs. It critically analyzes ethical concerns, implementation barriers and capacity gaps associated with AI adoption in education. The chapter proposes a conceptual framework linking AI integration, inclusive pedagogy and institutional outcomes. It further provides actionable suggestions for stakeholders seeking to leverage AI for sustainable disability support and improved institutional effectiveness.

items.title: AI‐Guided Intrinsic and Extrinsic Photocorrosion Inhibition of III–V Semiconductors for Durable Photoelectrochemical Water Splitting
items.abstract: Group III–V semiconductors are suitable for solar‐driven hydrogen production due to precise lattice matching (for tandem device combinations), high carrier mobilities (>10 3 cm 2 V –1 s –1 ), tunable bandgaps (1.1–2.5 eV), strong absorption coefficients (>10 5 cm –1 ), and a large range of doping possibilities. GaInP 2 , GaAs, and InP have a theoretical solar‐to‐hydrogen efficiency of more than 20%. Still, their high susceptibility to chemical and photochemical corrosion during prolonged photoelectrochemical water splitting (PEC‐WS) is a major industrial hurdle. This review comprehensively covers critical strategies to enhance the photostability of group III–V semiconductors for industrial‐scale PEC‐WS, emphasizing artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) support. We discuss three main intrinsic and extrinsic strategies that include (i) AI‐driven crystal structure modification and faceted growth control, (ii) physical and chemical surface passivation coupled with machine learning for passivation material screening strategies, and (iii) combining III–V semiconductors with appropriate band‐aligned materials via preferable heterojunctions, utilizing algorithms to select optimal compositions. We examine the underlying mechanisms of each strategy and conclude with perspectives on achieving optimal materials for PEC‐WS using advanced AI and ML screening tools. Implementing these effective modification strategies, the wide commercial potential of III–V photoelectrodes for PEC‐WS technology can be unlocked.

items.title: AI4AI: Toward AI-Discovered Superintelligence
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping how AI itself is developed. From designing learning algorithms to automating research workflows and evaluation, this expanding role has fueled the rapid growth of AI for AI (AI4AI). Yet a fundamental question remains: as AI takes on more research tasks, which decisions does it actually control? Even systems that execute entire research workflows may still rely on humans to define research goals, allowable modifications, and criteria for success. Existing taxonomies, typically organized by technique or target artifact, offer limited insight into these differences in research responsibility. This survey presents a unified, control-centered perspective on AI4AI, viewing its evolution as a progressive transfer of control over three key decisions in the discovery loop: search direction, search space, and evaluation signal. We introduce an L0–L3 control-source framework, complemented by full responsibility profiles, to characterize different forms of human–AI research responsibility without conflating control with overall capability or end-to-end autonomy. This perspective unifies research across AI4AI Learning, Inference, Data, and Infrastructure, while motivating an evaluation framework that goes beyond downstream performance to assess decision quality, discovery efficiency, transfer, evaluator independence, and robustness under optimization. Looking further ahead, AI4AI may enable recursive self-improvement, where advances in AI enhance the process of making subsequent discoveries. If sustained and independently validated, such improvements could offer a pathway toward superintelligence. By connecting research autonomy with the conditions for reliable and cumulative progress, this survey provides a unified foundation for understanding the evolution and long-term potential of AI4AI.

items.title: Algorithmic HRM and freelancer capabilities in Sri Lanka: constraints and the role of social support
items.abstract: Purpose This study examines how algorithmic human resource management (HRM) constrains the capabilities of platform-based freelancers in Sri Lanka, and how informal social support helps them sustain these capabilities. Design/methodology/approach Using a qualitative design, the research draws on 41 in-depth interviews and applies reflexive thematic analysis, informed by the capability approach and social support theory. Findings Four interconnected themes were identified: algorithmic work allocation constrains income security and temporal autonomy, digital enforcement and dispute processes undermine procedural fairness and recognition, artificial intelligence (AI)-driven market changes constrain capabilities through skill devaluation, and informal social support functions as an extra-platform capability infrastructure. Practical implications The findings point to implications for platform design, regulatory policy and emerging forms of worker organising, particularly in contexts marked by weak institutional protections. Originality/value This study draws on the capability approach and social support theory to make two contributions. First, it identifies a cumulative, reputation-based pathway through which algorithmic HRM constrains capabilities in knowledge-intensive freelancing. This extends current understanding beyond the transaction-based gig work that has dominated prior research. Second, it shows that informal social support contributes directly to capability development but cannot alter the structural algorithmic mechanisms that govern visibility, income security and procedural voice.

items.title: Algorithmic management and occupational health and safety: Non-deterministic insights into a contested relation
items.abstract: This article examines the relationship between algorithmic management and occupational health and safety (OHS) through the lens of Labour Process Theory, situating technology within the contested terrain of workplace control. Debates often isolate algorithmic management from the structural dynamics of managerial prerogative, overlooking how they relate to OHS risks. Using data from an European representative survey, this exploratory study assesses how automated work attribution and biological indicators monitoring condition workplace risks. Findings show divergent moderating patterns: these tools are associated with lower probabilities of detrimental OHS outcomes in some configurations, but higher probabilities in others. The moderating role of these tools varies considerably across different work environment configurations, and the magnitude of the associated shifts in probability is never enough to equalise scenarios where “traditional” risks are absent. Ultimately, the integration of technology can only be successful when done critically and without losing sight of broader workplace sources of risk.

items.title: Alignment in Multimodal Large Language Models: A Survey
items.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can generate fluent responses but may overlook relevant evidence or violate task and safety constraints. This survey examines MLLM alignment through two complementary gaps: the Modality Gap, concerning cross-modal correspondence and the use of task-relevant evidence, and the Intent Gap, concerning behavior relative to specified goals, constraints, and human expectations. We organize the literature along six dimensions: architecture, objective functions, data construction, training, evaluation, and applications. Across these dimensions, we link alignment mechanisms and supervision assumptions to the failures they target and the evidence supporting their effectiveness. Our analysis clarifies what interface compatibility, target imitation, preference learning, and verifiable rewards can each demonstrate about alignment, together with the limitations of their underlying supervision. We further summarize evaluation at the representation, task, and behavior levels, emphasizing evidence dependence, constraint compliance, and the distinction between observed improvements and explanations of their underlying mechanisms. Applications in robotics, safety, healthcare, recommendation, and climate decision support reveal three recurring requirements: traceable evidence, valid supervision, and decisions that respect domain constraints. Building on this synthesis, we identify four research directions: evidence-consistent alignment across modalities, verified self-correction and test-time alignment, diagnosis-guided repair, and reliable transfer to underrepresented settings.

items.title: Alternative creativity: why generative AI is creative, and why it is not like us
items.abstract: Abstract Whether generative artificial intelligence is creative is usually argued as a yes-or-no question, and both camps share an unexamined assumption, that there is one kind of creativity, the human kind, which the machine either has or lacks. This article defends a third position, alternative creativity. For any fixed medium the set of possible artefacts is finite and astronomically large, and almost none of it is valuable. Creativity, wherever it occurs, is therefore a compression of that space into a small manifold of meaningful candidates, followed by a value-guided search across the manifold. On the leading neuroscientific account, human brains work this way, and generative models demonstrably do. Neither creates from nothing, both recombine what they have internalised, both use constrained randomness, and both hold their skills in the strengths of their connections. In these respects the two are less different than is commonly supposed. Where they differ is in how the connections were shaped and in what each creator can reach at the moment of creation. A person's parameters are formed by a body acting in a physical and social world, a model's by an archive of what people have said and shown, and this difference in accessible context, together with a difference in how value is grounded, explains more of the divergence in what the two creators make than the difference of substrate does. In domains with checkable answers, machines already search beyond the human distribution under verifiable rewards. In the arts, where no verifier exists, they must borrow taste from people. From this account the article derives the homogenisation of machine output, the general intractability of tracing outputs to training inputs, the migration of authorship towards the specification of value, and the logic of human–machine collaboration, in which each creator supplies what the other constitutionally cannot.

items.title: An agentic AI system enhances clinical detection of immune-related adverse events in a multi-phase validation study
items.abstract: Abstract Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) affect up to 40% of patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors, yet identification requires laborious, inconsistent manual chart review. Here we show that agentic artificial intelligence coupled with human verification could enhance efficiency, performance and consistency for irAE assessment. We developed and evaluated an agentic large language model system to extract the presence, temporality, severity grade, attribution and certainty of six irAE types from clinical notes. Retrospectively, the system achieved a macro-averaged F 1 of 0.92 for current-event detection and 0.66 for multi-class severity grading; self-consistency improved F 1 by 0.14. The best-performing configuration cost approximately US$0.02 per note. In prospective silent deployment over 3 months, the binary F 1 was 0.72–0.79. In a randomized crossover study of clinical trial staff, agentic assistance reduced annotation time by 2.71 min ( P < 0.001), increased complete-match accuracy (odds ratio 1.45; 95% confidence interval 1.01–2.08; P = 0.045) and improved interannotator agreement (Krippendorff’s α from 0.22–0.51 to 0.82–0.85).

items.title: An AHP Framework for Evaluating Large Language Models in Software Vulnerability Assessment
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can assist software security review, but detecting more weaknesses may increase false alarms, unreliable patches, or higher costs. This methodological paper specifies a reproducible Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) framework for evaluating LLM-assisted vulnerability assessment in a synthetic banking-information application. Applying the framework to a local operational banking system was not feasible because obtaining the required security approvals was difficult; no production banking infrastructure was tested. Six objectives are linked to measurable indicators covering ground-truth completeness, detection, classification and severity assessment, secure remediation, reliability and resource use, and decision sensitivity. The protocol specifies 12 vulnerable and 12 corrected variants, four scenarios, repeated runs, blinded adjudication, CVSS v4.0 assessment, regression tests, and paired analysis. A comparison with SecurityEval, CyberSecEval, CyberSecEval 2, and BountyBench positions the proposed contribution as linking verified outcomes to stakeholder priorities rather than demonstrating superior benchmark performance. An exact reciprocal AHP example uses weights of 0.40, 0.30, 0.20, and 0.10. A separate simulation yields group weights of 0.3565, 0.2920, 0.2187, and 0.1328, with a consistency ratio of 0.0008. These are constructed examples, not elicited expert judgments. No LLM benchmarking was performed, and no model ranking is claimed. Empirical validation requires archived runs, independently assessed outcomes, and human stakeholder judgments; production transfer additionally requires institutional authorization and service-specific validation.

items.title: An Explainable AI Framework for Detecting Fraudulent Internship and Job Offers
items.abstract: Online portals have become commonplace for internships and job opportunities. With the increasing number of fraudulent internship and job offers, students find it difficult to differentiate between legitimate opportunities. Students face various risks such as fake recruiters, phishing, registration fee frauds, unrealistic offers, and other deceptions. This paper presents a study on an explainable artificial intelligence approach to detect fraudulent internship and job offers. It reviews existing artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, natural language processing, and transformer based recruitment fraud detection algorithms and techniques and explainability methods such as SHAP and LIME for providing an interpretable explanation for a model’s outcome. It highlights the limitations of previous approaches such as using generic datasets and lacking internship-specific features, limited explainability and no user-centric explanations.

items.title: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Correlational Study of Students' Perceptions Following an AI-Supported Gamified Formative-Assessment Intervention
items.abstract: Abstract Against the growing integration of artificial intelligence in higher education, this study examines the mechanism through which AI-supported gamification is associated with language learning outcomes in university language courses in the Greater Bay Area. Drawing on self-determination theory and a formative assessment perspective, it develops and tests a conceptual model linking gamification attitudes, learning motivation, perceived AI use, and perceived language learning improvement. A quantitative survey yielded 72 valid responses. The measurement scale showed good internal consistency . In addition, a post-hoc power analysis using G*Power 3.1 indicated that, with , , and a moderate effect size , statistical power reached .90, suggesting that the sample size was adequate for regression-based analysis. The results showed that gamification attitudes were significantly and positively associated with perceived language learning improvement, while learning motivation was moderately and positively associated with improvement. Mediation analysis indicated that learning motivation significantly predicted perceived language learning improvement . After learning motivation was included in the model, the direct effect of gamification attitudes was no longer significant, and bootstrap analysis supported a full mediation pattern. Although perceived AI use did not show a significant direct effect on perceived language learning improvement, AI remained an important supportive element in the intervention. In this study, AI was embedded in a recurring feedback-revision-practice-diagnosis-reinforcement cycle, providing individualized formative feedback and informing subsequent gamified practice and teacher guidance. Overall, the findings suggest that AI-supported gamification may contribute to language learning outcomes primarily through its relationship with students’ learning motivation. The study offers practical implications for the design of motivation-oriented, AI-supported formative assessment in higher education language learning contexts.

items.title: An Extended Adaptive Cuckoo Search Technique for Test Case Optimization
items.abstract: Model-driven test case production using Unified Modeling Language (UML) models has been widely explored to support early testing, often before system implementation. However, many existing techniques still struggle to produce optimal results efficiently, requiring a large number of iterations while achieving limited test coverage, as they rely on only a few UML models. To address these limitations, this study proposes an Extended Adaptive Cuckoo Search Technique (EACST), which builds and improves the Adaptive Cuckoo Search Algorithm (ACSA). Guided by the Design Science Research Methodology, the technique was conceptualized, developed, and evaluated through comparative experiments involving the Adaptive Cuckoo Search Algorithm (ACSA), the Enhanced Cuckoo Search Algorithm (ECSA), the hybrid Artificial Bee Colony and Simulated Annealing algorithm (ABC_SA), the Hybrid Graph-based Genetic Algorithm (HGGA), and the Differential Evolution algorithm with exponential crossover based on a learning strategy within the difference vector (DLS_DE). The initial evaluation was conducted using a single dataset to assess baseline performance under controlled conditions. The results demonstrate that EACST achieves optimal solutions using fewer iterations and reduced execution time compared to baseline techniques. Statistical validation using the Friedman and Wilcoxon tests further confirms these improvements, showing that EACST significantly outperforms ACSA, ECSA, ABC_SA, HGGA and DLS_DE. To ensure generalizability, a cross-system evaluation involving ten datasets was subsequently performed. The results show that EACST consistently generates a minimal test suite with maximum coverage, reduced effort, and fewer iterations compared to existing techniques. The proposed technique can be applied to a wide range of systems, including real-time environments such as Internet of Things systems and autonomous vehicles that utilize object-oriented paradigms. Future work will focus on developing hybrid approaches by integrating the proposed technique with Large Language Models and Reinforcement Learning to further enhance performance.

items.title: An SSA-to-ADR Uncertainty Propagation Pipeline for Tether-Net Debris Capture Mission Planning
items.abstract: Tether-net capture and Space Situational Awareness (SSA) have developed as separate disciplines, and capture-dynamics studies almost universally prescribe a deterministic target state. This paper proposes an end-to-end SSA-to-ADR uncertainty propagation pipeline treating tether-net capture as a probabilistic decision problem conditioned on observational data quality. Three stages are coupled: characterisation of the debris state covariance from TLE and photometric light-curve data; propagation of that covariance to the ejection epoch through a state transition matrix and drag-driven process noise; and construction of a capture probability surface over the ejection parameter space. Applied to Telkom-3 (NORAD 38744) over eleven epochs, the framework shows that SSA data quality governs capture performance through the validity horizon of the predicted state, not through terminal navigation accuracy. The two branches differ by two to three orders of magnitude: the translational horizon is eight to nine hours (8.0–9.3 h), whereas the rotational horizon falls from 115 to 23 s across three analysis epochs as the spin period shortens from 20.3 to 11.8 s. Capture probability at a 30 s observation-to-ejection latency drops correspondingly from 0.90 to 0.36. Photometric support must therefore be obtained minutes, not hours, before ejection, and the ejection timed to within about a second of the predicted favourable rotational phase.

items.abstract: Ketidakpatuhan penggunaan Alat Pelindung Diri (APD) di area pemilahan sampah manual Tempat Pembuangan Akhir (TPA) memicu risiko kecelakaan kerja dan penyakit akibat kerja yang tinggi. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengkuantifikasi risiko serta mengidentifikasi akar masalah sistemik ketidakpatuhan APD massal (±50% pekerja) melalui pendekatan hibrida Root Cause Analysis (RCA) Level 4, Human Factors Analysis and Classification System (HFACS), dan Fuzzy Fault Tree Analysis (FFTA). Data faktual diaudit melalui triangulasi lima jenis data dan disaring menggunakan KNOT Chart, dengan jumlah responden 30 pekerja (50% dari populasi), dan 4 orang pakar dari bidang K3 dan operasional. Struktur kausalitas diklasifikasikan ke dalam empat tingkatan HFACS dan dikuantifikasi menggunakan Triangular Fuzzy Numbers (TFN) berbasis konsensus pakar. Hasil kuantifikasi menunjukkan nilai probabilitas terjadinya ketidakpatuhan massal (Top Event) sebesar P(TE) = 5,69%. Akar masalah paling kritis teridentifikasi pada level Organizational Influences (BE4: sistem pengadaan kaku tahunan tanpa buffer stock, FPV = 0.058) dan Unsafe Supervision (BE7: ketiadaan SOP Progressive Disciplinary System, FPV = 0.048). Berdasarkan temuan tersebut, dirumuskan matriks rekomendasi terintegrasi berbasis Hierarchy of Controls dan CAPA 4-Level untuk mentransformasi sistem pengawasan serta logistik K3 secara permanen dan berkelanjutan.

items.title: Antimicrobial effect of essential oil of Gallesia integrifolia (Phytolaccaceae) against bacteria and fungi on hatching eggshells and its influence on the production parameters of day-old chicks
items.abstract: Formaldehyde-based disinfectants, although widely used for hatching egg sanitation and pathogen control in poultry production, pose serious occupational health risks and face increasing consumer opposition, driving the search for eco-friendly alternatives. In this context, this study aimed to evaluate the potential of Gallesia integrifolia (Phytolaccaceae) fruit essential oil, known for its antibacterial and antifungal properties, as a natural biocide for eggshell disinfection. For the experiment, 192 eggs were selected from the nests of two breeder houses located in the northwestern region of the state of Paraná. The selected eggs were divided into control and treatment groups and identified using sequential numbers in groups of four eggs. Eggs in the control group were disinfected by spraying them with an aqueous solution containing 2% polysorbate at a rate of 2 mL per egg. Eggs in the treatment group were disinfected with an aqueous solution containing 2% polysorbate and G. integrifolia essential oil at a concentration of 0.44 mg mL-1. The efficacy of G. integrifolia essential oil was assessed by counting aerobic mesophiles and fungi on the eggshell surface. The eggs were incubated, and the production and quality parameters of the hatched chicks were evaluated using scores. The results showed that G. integrifolia fruit essential oil did not alter the evaluated production parameters. Aerobic mesophile counts, chick quality scores, the egg weight-to-chick weight ratio, total hatchability, and hatchability of fertile eggs did not differ significantly (p ³ 0.05) between treatments in either breeder house. However, fungal counts in the first breeder house differed significantly (p < 0.05) between the treatment and control groups.

items.title: APLICAÇÕES DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NA DETECÇÃO PRECOCE DA SEPSE PEDIÁTRICA: UMA REVISÃO SISTEMÁTICA
items.abstract: A sepse é uma das principais causas de morbimortalidade pediátrica em serviços de urgência. Seu diagnóstico precoce permanece desafiador devido à apresentação clínica inespecífica e à rápida evolução da doença. Nesse contexto, modelos de inteligência artificial (IA), especialmente baseados em machine learning e deep learning, têm sido propostos como ferramentas de apoio à decisão clínica para identificação precoce de pacientes em risco. Portanto, torna-se necessário avaliar o desempenho e a aplicabilidade de modelos de IA na detecção precoce da sepse pediátrica em cenários de urgência e emergência. Trata-se de uma revisão sistemática conduzida conforme as diretrizes PRISMA. A busca foi realizada no PubMed utilizando os descritores “artificial intelligence”, “machine learning”, “deep learning”, “pediatric sepsis” e “childhood sepsis”, abrangendo os últimos 10 anos. Foram incluídos estudos originais envolvendo pacientes de 0 a 18 anos com modelos de IA aplicados à sepse pediátrica. Dos 38 estudos identificados, 10 atenderam aos critérios de elegibilidade. Os estudos demonstraram desempenho consistente na predição precoce da sepse, com AUROC entre 0,80 e 0,92 e antecipação diagnóstica de 2 a 6 horas. Modelos que integraram variáveis clínicas e laboratoriais, especialmente XGBoost e redes neurais recorrentes, apresentaram maior acurácia. Estratégias baseadas exclusivamente em sinais vitais contínuos mostraram desempenho satisfatório, monitorização em tempo real e maior aplicabilidade em ambientes com recursos limitados. Apesar dos resultados promissores, persistem limitações relacionadas ao desenho retrospectivo, amostras reduzidas e heterogeneidade metodológica.

items.title: Apple Vision Pro: The good, the bad, the ugly
items.abstract: Apple Vision Pro (AVP), the headset Apple introduced as its first ``spatial computer,'' built by a single, vertically integrated vendor, entered the market in February 2024 and has since accumulated a fast-growing body of primary research spanning surgery, education, accessibility, design, and human-computer interaction. In this paper, we adopt the tripartite structure of Leone's 1966 film to organize a systematic review of this literature: we cataloged the validated, working applications of AVP (the good), the persistent technical and ergonomic limitations of a still-early-generation headset (the bad), and the ethical concerns and structural harms that follow from deliberate design, marketing, and deployment choices (the ugly). The review is built from a Scopus export of 218 records mentioning AVP, which we narrowed to 104 papers (2024--2026) with a primary focus on AVP, using explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria that we report in full, alongside a PRISMA-informed flow diagram of the screening process. We find the corpus heavily skewed toward validating benefits (medicine and surgery, education, and software tooling account for over half of the included papers) and comparatively thin on documented risks or misuse, a pattern we treat as a finding in its own right rather than a limitation to be explained away. We further show that several recurring issues, namely price, simulated social presence, and the gaze-tracking privacy architecture, resist a clean separation into ``bad'' or ``ugly'' using the published evidence alone, since both readings remain compatible with the same data. We close by identifying where the evidence base most needs to grow: independent risk and ethics research, bystander- and equity-focused study designs, and disclosure that would let researchers distinguish an engineering backlog from a structural choice.

items.title: Applications, ethics, and future agenda of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in tourism and hospitality: a systematic review
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is reshaping how tourism information is produced, exchanged, and consumed, yet its application scenarios, ethical consequences, and implications for service authenticity remain dispersed across a fast-growing literature. Following the PRISMA 2020 protocol, this study identifies 3,825 records from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus and conducts a thematic synthesis of 461 publications, addressing three questions: where GenAI creates value on the supply and demand sides of tourism and hospitality, which ethical risks and organizational dilemmas accompany its adoption, and how machine intervention conflicts with interactional authenticity in service encounters. The synthesis indicates that GenAI operates as a double-edged sword. On the demand side, conversational and multimodal systems lower information search and decision-making costs; on the supply side, automated content generation unlocks operational capacity—yet these gains coexist with algorithmic bias and hallucination, privacy trade-offs, and employee deskilling. In service interactions, the computational essence of machine-generated empathy can elicit expectancy violations and algorithm aversion, weakening the interpersonal authenticity on which hospitality depends. The review integrates these findings into an efficacy-risk hedging framework embedded in a socio-technical account of human-AI collaboration and derives a tiered human-in-the-loop governance model. Its primary contribution is to link application-level benefits, systemic risks, and the authenticity conflict within one evidence-based framework, with each claim anchored in article-level evidence counts.

items.title: ARBITRA: Robust Document-Level ATT&CK Extraction via Multi-Expert Argumentation
items.abstract: Cyber threat intelligence (CTI) reports describe adversary behavior in natural language, but converting them into structured MITRE ATT&CK mappings remains difficult: existing methods decompose reports to sentence-level granularity for extraction, while modern LLMs can work with full reports in a single pass but with noticeable performance degradation. We present ARBITRA, which orchestrates multiple role-specialized LLM experts that propose candidate ATT&CK entities from the full report, which are then verified through a per-candidate quantitative bipolar argumentation framework (QBAF) grounded in document evidence and rationales. We additionally construct reasoning-specialized corpora for fine-tuning so experts can act as effective participants during this verification process. Across ATT&CK extraction benchmarks, ARBITRA reaches a stronger precision-oriented operating point than sentence-level pipelines, recent LLM-based extraction systems, and frontier models including GPT-5.5. Under adversarial perturbations simulating conflicting TTP statements, cross-report contamination, and semantic poisoning, ARBITRA limits mean precision degradation to roughly half that of frontier-model baselines for a more robust extraction.

items.title: Artificial intelligence (AI) proposals to counter AI cheating by students in non-invigilated assessment
items.abstract: Since ChatGPT3′s chatbot interface appeared in November 2022, AI cheating has re-incarnated a challenge for academia. It is accentuated in non-invigilated contexts during term as projects, essays and other documents are submitted (possibly) prior to proctored examinations. Cheating can be interpreted strategically as the institutional level, whereas its tactical expression examined in this article applies at the student-instructor interface. Here, we turn AI upon itself to see if it can address the dilemma it has created. A literature review regarding AI-facilitated cheating precedes a record of public and initial academic reactions. Having calibrated the problem, a method for addressing it is advanced. It enlists a set of AI large language models (LLMs) and search engines to rank six techniques by effectiveness in countering AI cheating. Analysis includes: descriptive assessment of model outputs; frequency counting, ranking and determination of unique and common techniques; and qualitative comparison of the suggestions tendered. The discussion relates the characteristics of the composite approaches to traditional assessment and evaluation. Ideas for ongoing research, and key recommendations form the conclusions.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Government Financial Reporting Transparency: Evidence from Nigeria's Federal Public Sector
items.abstract: Transparency is widely expected to sustain public trust in government, and artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly proposed as a means of making public financial information more open, timely and understandable. This study examines whether the overall level of documented AI adoption is associated with the transparency of government financial reporting in Nigeria's federal public sector, and what the evidence implies for public trust. A balanced panel of five federal institutions: the Federal Ministry of Finance, the Office of the Accountant-General of the Federation, the Federal Inland Revenue Service, the Central Bank of Nigeria and the Bureau of Public Procurement were observed from 2015 to 2024. Documentary evidence from annual reports, audit-related documents and AI-implementation documents is scored on a five-point (0–4) rubric and analysed with pooled, fixed-effects, trend-adjusted, first-difference and lagged regressions, interpreted through agency theory. Overall AI adoption is positively and significantly associated with transparency and credibility of financial reports (pooled β = 0.701, R² = 0.810; fixed-effects β = 0.708). Unlike the study's other AI–outcome relationships, however, this one is not robust throughout: the trend-adjusted coefficient (0.616) is only marginally significant (p = 0.051), and the first-difference coefficient (0.604) is not statistically significant (p = 0.112), although the lagged estimate (0.599) is. Transparency also has the lowest mean score of the five outcomes. The outcome is a documentary score of openness and credibility, not a survey of citizens, so the results speak to the supply of transparency and cannot establish public trust itself. Because the design is observational, the measures are documentary indices, and the sample is small and purposively selected, the results indicate association rather than proven causation and are interpreted for the five institutions examined rather than for all federal ministries, departments and agencies. AI adoption appears to be a helpful but insufficient condition for transparent reporting; communication, civic capacity and audit validation matter too.

items.abstract: Progressively, Human Resource Management (HRM) is using artificial intelligence (AI) to improve hiring, performance assessments, and employee engagement. This is especially true in developing countries that are slowly becoming more digital. Nonetheless, there is insufficient information about the influence of AI-driven HR initiatives on individual employee performance. A major flaw in present research is that it mostly looks at how well organizations succeed instead of how well employees do. This study offers a conceptual framework based on the Resource-Based View (RBV), examining the impact of AI integration in Human Resource Management (HRM) on employee performance, with employee engagement acting as a mediating variable. A standardized questionnaire was employed to gather data from 342 individuals involved in emerging economies where AI is being integrated. This was accomplished through a quantitative research methodology. We did the investigation using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The results show that using AI in HRM greatly improves how well employees do their jobs. Worker involvement is a partial mediator of this relationship, which means that AI technologies increase performance by making operations more efficient and getting workers more involved. The results show managers how to leverage AI-driven HR tools in a sensible way to get more work done by their employees and stay ahead of the competition.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Corporate ESG Performance: Causal Evidence from Machine Learning Methods
items.abstract: This study examines the effect of artificial intelligence (AI) innovation on corporate ESG performance in Chinese listed firms. Using 42,996 firm-year observations of 4792 A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2023, we measure AI innovation by AI patent applications and ESG performance by Huazheng ESG ratings. Two-way fixed effects estimates indicate that a one-unit increase in ln(1 + AI patent applications) is associated with a 0.037-point increase in the ESG score, or about 5% of a standard deviation for a one-standard-deviation increase in AI. Double/Debiased Machine Learning (DML) estimates with firm-level cross-fitting are similar (0.026–0.038). The relationship is robust to lagged AI, predetermined controls, ordinal and rank-based outcomes, and an event-study design that shows no differential ESG trends before firms’ first AI patent application; however, it is driven by the intensity of AI patenting rather than by the extensive margin and is imprecisely estimated within the pre- and post-2017 disclosure regimes. Mechanism tests suggest efficiency and internal-control channels, whereas the management expense ratio does not mediate the effect. The effect is stronger in larger firms and in firms with greater green innovation capability and tends to be larger in more market-oriented regions (significant at the 10% level), while the difference between heavily polluting and other firms is not statistically significant. Under a conditional exogeneity assumption, these results are consistent with a causal effect of AI innovation on ESG performance.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Financial Accountability in the Public Sector: Assessing Fraud Detection and Error Reduction in Nigeria's Federal Institutions
items.abstract: Public financial reports can fail through honest error as well as through deliberate manipulation, and both weaken accountability. This study examines whether documented adoption of artificial intelligence (AI)-based fraud detection systems is associated with error reduction and financial accountability in selected Nigerian federal public institutions. Drawing on a balanced panel of five purposively selected institutions observed from 2015 to 2024 (50 institution-year observations), the study codes official documents on a five-point (0–4) rubric and estimates pooled, fixed-effects, trend-adjusted, first-difference and lagged regressions, interpreted through agency theory. AI-based fraud detection is positively and significantly associated with error reduction and accountability (pooled β = 0.826; fixed-effects β = 0.865; within R² = 0.916). The association persists, but is smaller, after controlling for a common time trend (β = 0.560) and in first differences (β = 0.542), suggesting that part of the apparent effect reflects broader, simultaneous improvements in control environments. The findings support expanded and carefully governed use of AI-assisted anomaly detection in federal financial management, provided it is embedded in a functioning chain of review, triage and investigation, while cautioning against reading the coefficients as causal effects or generalising them to the wider federal sector

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and firm total factor productivity: evidence from digital capital accumulation and labour structure adjustment
items.abstract: Drawing on an unbalanced panel of Chinese A-share listed manufacturing firms from 2010 to 2020, this study examines the relationship between firm-specific artificial intelligence capability and total factor productivity (TFP), the accompanying capital and labour adjustments, and heterogeneity across industrial contexts and AI subfields. Using a patent-based measure of AI capability, we estimate firm-level models with high-dimensional fixed effects, while a staggered pilot-zone design provides quasi-experimental corroboration. Stronger AI capability is associated with higher TFP, greater intangible investment, higher headcounts of highly educated employees, and lower headcounts of less-educated employees. The productivity relationship is stronger in high-technology manufacturing and in industries with broader digital application scenarios, while machine learning exhibits the most stable positive association among AI subfields. Reweighting the listed sample to match the official distributions of firm size, industry, and ownership among above-scale manufacturing enterprises leaves the estimate essentially unchanged. The findings document a positive within-firm AI–TFP relationship among listed manufacturers.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning in Plant Breeding: Data-driven Frameworks for Genomic Prediction, High-throughput Phenotyping and Accelerated Cultivar Development
items.abstract: Plant breeding is increasingly a data-intensive science. Modern programmes generate genome-wide marker data, multi-environment trial records, remote-sensing and sensor streams, and high-resolution images at a scale that exceeds the capacity of conventional statistical workflows. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) offer a set of tools for extracting predictive signal from such data. This review surveys the application of ML and deep learning across the breeding cycle, beginning with the foundations of the main algorithm families and moving to genomic selection, where linear mixed models remain the benchmark against which random forests, support vector machines, neural networks and convolutional architectures are measured. It then considers image-based high-throughput phenotyping and disease detection, modelling of genotype-by-environment interaction and integration with crop growth models, yield prediction, optimisation of training populations and trial design, and the coupling of predictive models with genome editing. Deep learning is most firmly established for image- and sensor-based phenotyping, although generalisation across sites remains a recognised weakness, whereas the advantage of ML over well-specified linear models for genomic prediction of complex traits is modest and context dependent. Key obstacles include small sample sizes relative to the number of predictors, limited model interpretability, data heterogeneity, and unequal access to computing and expertise.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Techniques in Financial Forecasting
items.abstract: This study provides a comprehensive bibliometric analysis of 2,226 journal articles published between 2005 and 2025 to address the following research question: What is the academic landscape of research on AI and ML models in financial forecasting? Descriptive analysis reveals publication trends, journal distributions, the most productive countries, institutions, and authors, as well as citation patterns within the field. Network analysis identifies five major research clusters and examines collaboration patterns among researchers and across countries and regions. Furthermore, the study explores the evolution of research topics and the thematic structure of the field through keyword and thematic analyses, highlighting key research trends and several promising directions for future research. The findings show a clear evolution from traditional AI and ML approaches towards deep-learning-driven forecasting, with growing research interest in cryptocurrencies and sentiment-based analysis.

items.title: Artificial intelligence and the spirit of assessment scholarship
items.abstract: In response to generative artificial intelligence (AI), assessment scholarship can be overlooked. This final chapter of the volume Designing University Assessment for a World With Artificial Intelligence outlines what our collected assessment scholarship has offered the readership. Drawing from Charles Dickens’s Christmas Carol as inspiration, I describe what we have learned from the scholarly ghosts of Assessment Past, Assessment Present, and Assessment Yet to Come. The ghosts of assessment scholarship provide answers to the following three questions: what does a university stand for in a time of AI, and what does this mean for assessment? What does it mean for a student to ‘do their own work’ in a time of AI? How does all this help an educator design assessment in a time of AI at scale, with no resources and no time? Drawing from the collection of chapters by eminent scholars, I offer theoretical insights and practical first steps but no easy solutions. However, I conclude, if we prioritise scholarly communality and conversation, we can avoid a Scrooge-like approach to assessment—diminished, ungenerous, and shaped by frugality above all things.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Applied to Echocardiography for Detection of Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction and Elevated Filling Pressures: A Diagnostic Test Accuracy Meta-Analysis
items.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) accounts for nearly half of heart failure cases and remains difficult to diagnose non-invasively. Artificial intelligence (AI) applied to echocardiography may improve detection, but its aggregate diagnostic accuracy has not been quantified. We performed a diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis of AI-enabled echocardiography for identifying HFpEF, elevated left ventricular filling pressure, or diastolic dysfunction. MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched from inception to June 2026. Studies reporting the accuracy of AI models applied to echocardiography against invasive, guideline-adjudicated, or ASE/EACVI reference standards were included. Sensitivity and specificity were pooled using a bivariate random-effects (Reitsma) model, with a summary receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, diagnostic odds ratio, and likelihood ratios. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2. Eight studies (2770 participants; 1317 [47.5%] with the target condition) were included. Pooled sensitivity was 84.0% (95% CI: 73.0-91.0%) and specificity 83.0% (95% CI: 73.0-89.0%), with an area under the summary ROC curve of 0.875 (95% CI: 0.791-0.930). The diagnostic odds ratio was 24.73 (95% CI: 18.46-33.12); positive and negative likelihood ratios were 4.84 and 0.20. Heterogeneity was high. Performance did not differ by AI architecture but varied significantly by reference standard. No small-study effects were detected. AI-enabled echocardiography shows good pooled accuracy for detecting HFpEF and elevated filling pressures, supporting its diagnostic potential. High heterogeneity and reference-standard dependence warrant larger, prospectively validated studies before routine clinical adoption.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence for Predictive Microbiome Engineering: Integrating Community Design and Environmental Validation
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Microbial ecosystems can now be measured across genomic, transcriptomic, proteomic, metabolomic, and environmental dimensions, yet their emergent functions remain difficult to predict and control. Artificial intelligence (AI) can integrate heterogeneous data, but predictive accuracy alone does not establish causality, transferability, or controllability. This review developed a five‐layer framework: observe, infer, predict, design, and learn that connects microbial measurement to prospective intervention and experimental feedback. We critically synthesise evidence from sequence and protein learning, multi‐omics integration, metabolic modelling, synthetic microbial communities, environmental biotechnology, and temporal forecasting. Recent primary studies illustrate progress in forecasting community trajectories, predicting microbial competition and designing consortia for pollutant degradation; they also reveal important boundaries between model performance and demonstrated ecosystem control. We examine risks arising from compositional data, information leakage, dependent observations, batch effects, uncertain calibration, sparse perturbation data, ecological instability, and evolutionary change. We propose operational criteria for ecosystem programmability and a staged validation pathway from controlled systems to field‐relevant environments. Progress will depend on standardised context‐rich data, hybrid AI–mechanistic models, prospective benchmarks, independent replication, and safety‐constrained design.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Education: Opportunities, Challenges, and Implications for the Learning Process
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping education faster than pedagogical theory and institutional policy can absorb it. Although reviews of AI in education (AIEd) are multiplying, most catalogue applications or list risks separately, leaving unclear how opportunities and challenges jointly reconfigure the learning process. This study addresses that gap through a systematic literature review guided by the PRISMA 2020 statement. Records were identified through the Consensus academic search engine using two search strings and supplemented by citation searching, then screened against criteria covering publication between 2021 and 2026, peer-reviewed status, an active DOI, and direct relevance to teaching and learning. Twenty-four studies were retained and analysed through thematic synthesis. The results reveal four clusters of opportunity: personalised and adaptive learning, intelligent tutoring and feedback, AI-supported assessment, and augmentation of teachers' work. These are counterbalanced by five clusters of challenge: academic integrity, algorithmic bias and data privacy, overreliance and the erosion of higher-order thinking, unequal infrastructure and AI literacy, and weak institutional governance. Mapping both clusters onto the stages of the learning process, the study proposes a Learner–Teacher–AI Agency Framework, which holds that AI improves learning only when it redistributes, rather than replaces, human agency. Implications are drawn for pedagogy, assessment redesign, teacher professional development, and policy, particularly in developing-country contexts such as Indonesia.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in higher education and graduate employability: cognitive engagement, self-efficacy, and career adaptability in the AI era
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI), particularly generative AI, is increasingly used in higher education, but its contribution to graduate employability cannot be inferred from access to AI or frequency of use alone. This critical narrative review examines how AI-supported learning may relate to employability through processes discussed in educational psychology and career development. Searches of Web of Science, Scopus, ERIC, and PubMed covered database inception to 1 July 2026, with supplementary searches completed on 2 October 2026. The literature was synthesized interpretively and critically, with attention to the type of outcome measured and the extent to which findings support the proposed relationships. The synthesis focuses on cognitive engagement and self-regulated learning, self-efficacy and motivational regulation, and career adaptability. Three tensions organize the discussion: capability augmentation and cognitive offloading, career agency and AI-related insecurity, and resource access and capability differences. Included studies report associations or short-term changes in outcomes such as engagement, AI literacy, self-efficacy, career adaptability, and perceived employability. Direct evidence linking AI-supported learning to later employment outcomes remains limited. The proposed framework should therefore be read as a set of theory-informed pathways for future testing, rather than as an established causal or temporal sequence. Implications for assessment, disciplinary AI literacy, career education, institutional support, and future research are discussed.

items.abstract: ABSTRACT:Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative technology in pharmaceutical sciences andpharmacy practice, enabling the transition from conventional trial-and-error approaches to data-driven,predictive, and personalized healthcare solutions. This review critically examines the applications of AIthroughout the pharmaceutical and pharmacy continuum, encompassing drug discovery, formulationdevelopment, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic modeling, clinical decision support, supply chainmanagement, pharmacovigilance, and patient-centered care. Advanced AI methodologies, including machinelearning, deep learning, natural language processing, large language models, and computer vision, facilitatethe analysis of complex biomedical datasets, accelerate target identification, optimize molecular design,predict absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion, and toxicity (ADMET) properties, and supportprecision medicine initiatives. In clinical and community pharmacy settings, AI-driven systems enhancemedication safety, automate dispensing processes, improve inventory management, strengthen adverse drugreaction surveillance, and promote medication adherence through intelligent monitoring technologies and telepharmacy services. Despite these advantages, significant challenges remain, including data quality andinteroperability issues, algorithmic bias, limited model interpretability, concerns regarding privacy andcybersecurity, and evolving regulatory and ethical considerations. These barriers highlight the need for robustgovernance frameworks, transparent and explainable AI models, and rigorous validation strategies.Furthermore, AI is redefining the role of pharmacists by shifting professional responsibilities toward clinicaldecision-making, data analytics, multidisciplinary collaboration, and continuous patient care management.Future developments are expected to focus on explainable AI, federated learning, edge computing, hybridintelligence systems, and the integration of AI competencies into pharmacy education. Overall, the successfulimplementation of AI, coupled with human expertise and ethical oversight, has the potential to enhance theefficiency, safety, and personalization of pharmaceutical development and healthcare delivery, ultimatelyimproving patient outcomes and advancing the future of intelligent pharmacy practice.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Public Governance: Assessing Indonesia’s Readiness and Regulatory Framework
items.abstract: Governance constitutes a fundamental component of public administration and plays a decisive role in determining the quality, accessibility, and accountability of public services in Indonesia. As social needs and technological capabilities continue to evolve, the government is required to adapt its institutional structures, administrative mechanisms, and regulatory frameworks to ensure that public services remain effective, inclusive, and responsive. This requirement has become increasingly significant following the transformation of conventional government administration toward the Electronic-Based Government System (Sistem Pemerintahan Berbasis Elektronik or SPBE). Although digital transformation provides opportunities to improve administrative efficiency, transparency, and coordination, it also generates new challenges concerning state responsibility, data sovereignty, cybersecurity, personal data protection, and the safeguarding of citizens' rights in cyberspace. These challenges have become more complex with the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), which enables automated data processing, predictive analysis, and decision-support mechanisms within governmental institutions. Accordingly, this study examines the urgency of governmental adaptation and the strategies required to establish AI-based governance that is consistent with the principles of legality, accountability, transparency, social equity, and public welfare. This research employs a doctrinal legal research method through a literature-based study, utilizing statutory, conceptual, and analytical approaches to examine the relevant legal framework, governance principles, and implications of AI adoption in public administration. The findings indicate that AI offers substantial opportunities to improve the efficiency, accuracy, responsiveness, and accessibility of public services. Nevertheless, its implementation may also generate algorithmic bias, limited decision-making transparency, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, privacy violations, and uncertainty regarding legal responsibility for AI-assisted administrative decisions. These risks demonstrate that technological advancement alone cannot guarantee the realization of effective and accountable governance. Government readiness must therefore be strengthened through regulatory adaptation, institutional capacity-building, the development of secure and equitable digital infrastructure, continuous evaluation of AI systems, and meaningful public participation. Furthermore, Indonesia requires clearer legal standards governing the responsible use of AI, including human oversight, accountability mechanisms, data protection, and legal remedies for individuals affected by automated decisions. This study argues that the integration of AI into SPBE should be understood not merely as a technological modernization initiative but as a legal and institutional transformation that must remain oriented toward the public interest. Ultimately, adaptive AI-based governance requires a balanced approach that maximizes technological benefits while ensuring legal certainty, ethical responsibility, social inclusion, and the protection of fundamental rights in Indonesia's evolving digital society.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in the Boardroom Legal and Governance Consequences for Company Directors, with Reference to Uganda: A Systematic Review
items.abstract: Companies are adopting artificial intelligence (AI) in decisions that boards have traditionally taken, yet it is unclear what this means in law for company directors and no systematic review has examined the question for Uganda. This review identified, appraised and synthesised scholarly evidence on the legal and governance consequences of AI use for company directors, and on what the evidence implies for Ugandan directors. Following PRISMA 2020, Consensus (two searches, 40 records) and CORE (three searches, 300 records) were searched, and records were imported into Zotero on 27 October 2026. After 115 duplicates were removed, 225 unique records were screened and 36 reports were sought. Nine could be assessed and were included and 27 could not be retrieved. Studies were eligible if they analysed directors' duties, liability or board governance in relation to AI, in any jurisdiction, with priority given to Uganda and Africa. Quality was appraised with a six-domain instrument adapted from the JBI, CASP and AMSTAR 2 checklists and findings were synthesised thematically. The included studies were doctrinal and conceptual legal analyses from South Africa, Nigeria, Australia, Ireland, the European Union and the United States. Five themes emerged: liability remains with human directors because AI lacks legal personality; directors' duties of care and the business judgment rule govern reliance on AI; legal frameworks lag behind practice and give little guidance; replacing directors with AI is legally contested; and AI raises stakeholder and corporate purpose questions. No included study concerns Uganda, and none reports litigation or empirical evidence on how boards use AI. The evidence is largely conceptual, comes mainly from civil, statutory and common law systems other than Uganda's and is incomplete because most sought reports could not be retrieved. Priorities are doctrinal analysis of the Companies Act 2012 and the Data Protection and Privacy

items.title: Artificial intelligence-assisted intelligent detection model for microscopic defects in ultra-high voltage shielding clothing materials
items.abstract: Ultra-high voltage (UHV) transmission systems require shielding clothing with high conductivity, uniform structure, and stable electromagnetic protection to ensure operator safety. Microscopic defects like pinholes, micro-cracks, fiber fractures, and coating discontinuities severely reduce effectiveness and are difficult to detect with conventional manual inspection. This suggested model proves to be an efficient, energy-aware, reliable, and scalable solution for the intelligent quality assessment of the UHV shielding clothing manufacturing and maintenance processes. In particular, the AI-aided Intelligent Detection Model is created to automatize and improve the accuracy of classification of microscopic fabric defects, which can be used to detect fabric defects of UHV shielding clothing materials. For this experiment, the Kaggle Multi-Class Fabric Defect Detection Dataset has been used as a source, it includes 3077 images of microscopic fabric defects belonging to several classes of defects. These images belong to generic images of fabric defects and do not contain any information about UHV shielding clothing, conductive threads, or EM shielding deterioration. In this regard, the following results have been achieved with the accuracy (98.42%), precision (96.81%), recall (95.37%), F1-score (96.08%), and computational efficiency (97%). It proves to be an efficient tool to classify microscopic fabric defects, while further research can be dedicated to the application of this method to the classification of fabric defects of UHV shielding clothes.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Face Recognition Using Deep Learning - A Review of Models, System Design, Applications and Challenges
items.abstract: Face recognition has become one of the most widely deployed applications of artificial intelligence, supporting smartphone unlocking, attendance management, banking and border control. Deep learning has replaced hand-crafted features with representations learned directly from large collections of face images, producing large gains in accuracy under unconstrained conditions. This paper presents a structured review of artificial intelligence-based face recognition using deep learning. It explains the stages of a recognition pipeline, compares the main families of deep models and training objectives, proposes a modular system architecture with a liveness check, and summarizes datasets and evaluation measures. Application areas, including education and financial services, are discussed together with the main challenges: pose and occlusion, spoofing, demographic bias, adversarial attacks and privacy. The paper closes with emerging directions such as self-supervised learning, synthetic training data, federated learning and privacy-preserving matching, and offers practical recommendations for responsible deployment
